result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select all nodes within K hops of specified seed nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5647-L5738){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood( nodes, k=1, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uses breadth-first search to find neighbors at distance up to k from the seed nodes. Does not include the seed nodes themselves in the selection. Useful for extracting local neighborhoods. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Seed node(s) to start from. Can be a single node ID (int), a single label (str), or a list of node IDs/labels. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of hops/distance to traverse. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Direction to traverse: `"out"`, `"in"`, or `"all"`. For undirected graphs, always uses the `"all"` mode. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 5-node star, a 1-hop selection from the hub reaches every spoke, but not the hub itself, since seed nodes are excluded from the result: ::: {#2da4c87e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(n=5) center_id = list(graph.get_node_ids(limit=None))[0] graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood(nodes=center_id, k=1, mode="all") graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Increasing `k` extends the reach further along the graph. Starting from "A" with `k=2` and following outgoing edges reaches "B" and "C", but not "D", which is three hops away: ::: {#5d93473e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood(nodes="A", k=2, mode="out") [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['B', 'C', 'A'] ``` ::: ::: Multiple seed nodes are unioned together -- here, the 1-hop neighborhoods of both "A" and "B" combine, without including "A" or "B" themselves: ::: {#bdac5a1c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("A", "C") .add_edge("B", "D") .add_edge("C", "E") ) graph.select_nodes_in_neighborhood(nodes=["A", "B"], k=1, mode="all") [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['C', 'A', 'D', 'B'] ``` ::: :::
